newsitem.title: UK: Lithuania expected to launch dollar Eurobond soon.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania expected to launch dollar Eurobond soon.

text.p: Lithuania is expected to launch a planned dollar Eurobond soon after an investor presentation in London on Thursday, bankers close to the deal said on Monday.
The former Soviet republic is expected to launch a $200 million five-year bond via JP Morgan. Unofficial price talk is around 100 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
Earlier this month Standard & Poor's assigned an investment grade BBB- rating to Lithuania's long-term foreign curreny debt.
S&P said Lithuania's ratings reflected the government's commitment to market-based economic reforms, and its plans for accelerating the second phase of privatisation.
In September last year Moody's Investors Service assigned a below investment grade Ba2 rating to Lithuania's foreign currency debt.
Lithuania made its debut on international capital markets in December 1995, with a $60 million Eurobond with a two year maturity and a 10 percent coupon which was increased to total $110 million.
